questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Renewable energy is energy that is environment-friendly because it is ______ from renewable resources, that are naturally replenished.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**derived**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is about renewable energy and its characteristics.
 
• The correct verb should indicate the process of obtaining or sourcing energy from renewable resources.
 
• "**Derived**" (निकाला गया) means obtained from a specific source, which matches the context of renewable energy being sourced from resources that are naturally replenished.
 
• Other options ("**construed**" (समझा गया), "**deduced**" (निष्कर्ष निकाला), "**found**" (पाया)) do not fit as well in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *Renewable energy is energy that is environment-friendly because it is **derived__* * from renewable resources, that are naturally replenished.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Construed **(समझा गया): It means interpreted or understood in a particular way, which does not fit the context of how energy is obtained.
 
• **Deduced **(निष्कर्ष निकाला): It means concluded from reasoning, which is not related to the process of obtaining energy from renewable resources.
 
• **Found **(पाया): While it means discovered, it does not accurately describe the process of sourcing energy from renewable resources.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

'I have been to Australia,' Amritha told me.

options.text: Amritha told me that she had been to Australia.
Amritha told me that she has be to Australia.
Amritha told me that she had being to Australia.
Amritha tell me that she has being to Australia.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and needs to be converted into indirect speech.
 
• The verb "**have been**" in present perfect changes to "**had been**" in past perfect in indirect speech.
 
• The correct transformation is: "**Amritha told me that she had been to Australia.**"
 
• **Option 1** correctly follows these rules and accurately represents the indirect speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Amritha told me that she had been to Australia."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: ** "Amritha told me that she has be to Australia." – Incorrect because of the incorrect verb form "has be".
 
• **Option 3: ** "Amritha told me that she had being to Australia." – Incorrect grammar, "had being" is not correct.
 
• **Option 4: ** "Amritha tell me that she has being to Australia." – Incorrect subject-verb agreement and incorrect verb form "has being".

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The insect bit the little baby

options.text: The little baby was bitten by the insect.
The little baby is bitten by the insect.
The little baby has bitten by the insect.
The little baby had bitten by the insect.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To change an active voice sentence to passive voice, the object of the active sentence (the little baby) becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb "**bit**" in past simple is changed to "**was bitten**" in passive voice.
 
• The subject of the active sentence (the insect) becomes the agent of the passive sentence, introduced by "**by**".
 
• The correct passive sentence is: "**The little baby was bitten by the insect.**"

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The little baby was bitten by the insect."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: ** "The little baby is bitten by the insect." – Incorrect because it uses the present tense "is bitten" instead of past tense "was bitten".
 
• **Option 3: ** "The little baby has bitten by the insect." – Incorrect because "has bitten" is a present perfect form, which is not suitable here.
 
• **Option 4: ** "The little baby had bitten by the insect." – Incorrect because it incorrectly uses "had bitten" which is past perfect without the auxiliary "been".

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘decline’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Increase**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"decline"** means to decrease or deteriorate over time. (गिरावट)

 
 
• **Example: **The population of the endangered species continued to **decline **due to habitat loss.
 
 
 
• **"Increase" **means to become larger or greater in size, amount, or degree. (वृद्धि)
 
 
• **Example: **The company's profits saw a significant **increase **after the new marketing campaign.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'decline' **is **'increase'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Decrease **(कमी): To become smaller or less in size, amount, or degree.

 
 
• **Example:** The new law aims to **decrease **pollution levels in the city.
 
 
 
• **Drag **(खींचना): To pull something along forcefully, roughly, or with difficulty.
 
 
• **Example: **He had to **drag **the heavy suitcase up the stairs.
 
 
 
• **Push **(धक्का देना): To exert force on someone or something in order to move them away from oneself.
 
 
• **Example:** She had to **push **the door with all her might to get it open.
